svg.title: Payload encryption and message-kind routing: definition push vs. command push
svg.desc: Two WRP payload kinds -- a static definition push (protocol + toolset schema, no commands) and a dynamic command push (protocol + toolset + commands) -- are both encrypted at the payload level before being carried over TLS/WSS transport inside a WRP envelope. The device receives the envelope, decrypts the payload, and routes on message kind: a definition push goes to Plugin Manager to load/register the toolset; a command push goes over local JSON-RPC IPC into Execution Framework to actually run the command. This "static/dynamic" message-kind axis is adopted from the user-supplied diagram and is distinct from plugin_contract.h's load_type field (compiled-in vs dlopen), which describes how a plugin binary is loaded, not what kind of WRP message this is.
svg.text: Reconciled against the existing spec suite
1. Payload encryption is now required, layered under TLS/WSS transport (not transport
alone) — resolves OPEN_QUESTIONS.md C7. Every WRP payload is encrypted before it enters
the WRP envelope, both for toolset.push and for ordinary command traffic.
2. "Static" and "dynamic" here describe WRP MESSAGE KIND (definition push vs. command
push) — this is a different axis from plugin_contract.h's load_type field (compiled-in vs.
dlopen()), which describes how a plugin binary is loaded, not what kind of message this
is. Both a statically-loaded and a dynamically-loaded plugin can be the target of either a
definition push or a command push -- the two axes are independent, not the same thing.
3. The "static" branch (Load Plugins) is this diagram's version of toolset.push /
define-synchronous-toolset-push -- a definition/manifest arriving without an execution
request. The "dynamic" branch (JSON-RPC Local IPC -> Execute Commands) is the existing
§5.1 command-execution flow / tools/call, unchanged in substance, now explicitly shown
decrypting before Dispatch Core's ACL checkpoint runs.
4. Decryption happens in Dispatch Core, before the single ACL checkpoint (FR-4) --
encryption is a confidentiality control on the wire, not a substitute for authorization,
and does not change where or how ACL is evaluated.
